originality_rule: Each entry contributes an abstract IDEA (composition class, colour feeling, typographic attitude, pattern/texture language) with provenance. No artwork traced, reproduced, or closely derived; per-entry originality notes state what is taken and what is not.

entries.observed: From search snippet plus a partial fetch (page login-walled, only board title/organization retrievable): a 460-pin board of vintage face powder boxes and compacts. The search snippet for this and sibling boards described Art Deco fluted two-tone boxes, enamel leaf patterns, Victorian florals, and a 'garland of violets' powder box — i.e. the historical face-powder genre: a bordered, centered, softly ornamented lid face.
entries.idea_contributed: Composition class: the classic powder-box face — a delicate ornamental border or garland frame running the square lid's perimeter, enclosing a small centered word stack (BBROSE / FACE POWDER / POLVOS). Two-tone discipline of the era maps directly onto 621C ground + 627C ink. Reads as heritage complexion product, distinct from all five ES3083 directions.
entries.originality_note: Taken: only the genre convention (perimeter garland frame + centered modest wordmark on a pale two-tone ground). NOT taken: no specific vintage box's artwork traced or closely derived; any garland would be drawn fresh from BBROSE's own Damascena rose/leaf vocabulary.

The motif is felt more than seen: exactly the veil/skin-light softness a powder lid wants versus an eyeshadow lid.

entries.observed: Fetched the README summary. Tool converts raster images to SVG halftone: shapes circle/hex/diamond; grids rect/hex/diamond/poisson (poisson described as randomized, organic, naturalistic spacing); darker areas produce larger shapes, lighter areas smaller; invert and contrast options; vector output intended for laser cutting.
entries.idea_contributed: Density-gradient veil: a halftone-style dot field on a poisson (blue-noise) grid whose dot sizes fade smoothly from one edge or corner of the square toward a clear zone — reading as powder dusted across skin and thinning to bare complexion. The clear zone hosts the three words. Poisson spacing keeps it organic and cosmetic rather than mechanical/print-shop; single ink 627C on 621C ground.
entries.originality_note: Taking only the compositional class (size-graded dots on an organic grid) and the poisson-grid softness idea. No image would be converted and nothing generated by this tool would be used; the gradient ramp driving dot size would be defined mathematically by us, so the artwork shares no source material with the repo's outputs.

entries.observed: Fetched the README summary. HalftonePAL ('Halftone with Points and Lines') is a Processing tool with ten point-arrangement methods (circle packing tight/loose, random dithering, quadtree, error diffusion on square and hex grids) and eleven pattern styles, including 'tilted lines oriented to local gradients', scan-lines, nearest-3-neighbour lines, greedy paths, Hilbert ordering, MST, Voronoi, Delaunay; plotter-friendly output.
entries.idea_contributed: Directional nap: the 'tilted short lines oriented to a local gradient' style, abstracted into a field of hairline dashes whose angles rotate gently and coherently across the square — like the brushed nap of velvet or the sweep of a powder brush across a compact. Reads as sheen/direction rather than pattern; extremely quiet at 627C hairline weight on 621C, words placed where the nap 'parts'.
entries.originality_note: Taking only the abstract pattern language (short oriented strokes driven by a smooth angle field). Our angle field would be an original mathematical construction, not derived from any image or from this tool's output; no code or rendered artwork copied.

entries.observed: Fetched the README summary. StippleGen (Evil Mad Scientist) implements Weighted Voronoi Stippling: dots distributed by image brightness, variable dot sizes for gray levels, density rising in darker regions; also a TSP single-continuous-path variant; vector output for pen plotters.
entries.idea_contributed: Tone from density alone: an abstract soft circular bloom — the ghost of a puff pressed once onto the lid, slightly off-centre on the big square — rendered purely as stipple density with no outline or edge, dots thinning to nothing. Tone emerging from scattered points is exactly the face-powder register: skin-light, translucent, no drawn figure. Deliberately an abstract density field, not a stippled picture.
entries.originality_note: Taking only the algorithmic idea (weighted point density encodes tone). No photograph or reference image would be stippled — the density field would be an original analytic function (a soft radial falloff we define) — so nothing is traced, converted, or derived from any existing image or from this tool's example outputs.

entries.observed: From the search snippet: fast 2D Poisson disk sampling based on a modified Bridson algorithm, JavaScript, with configurable shape, radius, and tries parameters — i.e. blue-noise point sets with a guaranteed minimum spacing. Not fetched; observed from result listing only.
entries.idea_contributed: Loose-powder settle: a sparse, even-but-never-clumping scatter of specks across the whole lid at very low coverage — the way loose powder settles on a surface — using two vector speck vocabularies within the two-ink rule (tiny solid 627C dots plus slightly larger open 627C rings) so the field shimmers at two 'depths' without needing a third colour or tint screens. Generous minimum spacing is what makes it read as quiet luxury instead of texture noise.
entries.originality_note: Taking only the sampling concept (minimum-distance blue-noise scatter), a standard published algorithm (Bridson). No code from this library is required or copied; an original implementation with our own parameters produces the artwork.

entries.observed: From the search snippet: a curated list of code and resources for computer-controlled drawing machines; the result text notes it indexes tools such as 'Flow Lines', described as generating flow-line representations as SVG paths/polylines, alongside generative frameworks (e.g. go-pen with perlin-noise vector fields). entries.observed: From search snippet (not fetched): the quiet-luxury complexion register is described through product language — 'a buildable veil of color', 'second-skin coverage', 'money talks, wealth whispers' — classy, sheer, whisper-toned rather than declarative.

entries.originality_note: Taken: only the abstract tonal register ('veil', second-skin, whispered luxury) as an evaluation lens. NOT taken: no product design, brand identity, or image from the roundup is used or derived from.
